The logistic regression classifier operates by transforming a linear combination of inputs into a probability via the sigmoid function. This allows for probabilistic interpretation of outcomes such as medal wins. The negative log-likelihood loss serves as the objective function that guides parameter estimation by penalizing incorrect predictions more heavily when confidence is high. Weighted feature aggregation forms the basis of this transformation, combining multiple variables into a single scalar input for the classifier. Dualities emerge in how these components interact—linear aggregation enables non-linear decision boundaries through the sigmoid, while loss minimization ensures robustness against noise. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient regularization, misclassification from poor feature selection, and instability from extreme probability estimates near zero or one.
